column1: # Vendored-source manifest. Read by scripts/check-drift.*, which asks
# one question: has the upstream changed what we copied since we copied
# Written by scripts/sync-rgx-upstream.sh, not by hand: a manifest that
# falls behind the tree it describes is worse than none, because it
# The file holds two things: the rows, which are tab separated and
# five columns wide, and the excluded paths, which are comment
# lines of their own -- "# exclude: <path>", one per line. A
# comment line is not a row: the parsers skip the comments, and
#   1  rgx_path    the path in this repository. A tree row names a
#                   directory; a patch row names the patch file.
#   2  upstream    the path in the upstream rgx checkout.
#   3  pin         the upstream commit the copy was taken from.
#   5  note        why the row is here.
# The trees below are upstream rgx's crates: the copy of them, with
# this repository's patches on top. The licence follows upstream's.
# specification provenance of those files is upstream's own manifest
# (scripts/vendored-sources.tsv in the rgx checkout), and the
# third-party notices are in NOTICE and the licence files at the root.
# A patch row is a file of this repository that upstream does not
# have, or has differently: a divergence from upstream is a patch
# applied on top of the copy -- or, when upstream has no such path
# at all, a patch that creates the file -- and the patch is what
# says what the divergence is. The note on the row says which of
# the two it is. A tree that carries patches is not upstream's
# verbatim, and the patch rows below it are the ones that say so.
# A row whose note says the copy excludes paths is a tree that is
# upstream's minus what rgy does not carry: upstream's benchmark
# harnesses and its fuzzing crate, which rgy does not run. The
# exclusion is in the sync script, so the paths cannot come back.
# The upstream commit the copy was taken from: 8c32dc09b048c93bfff0579a7386307a39719e5e
# The paths the copy does not carry, one per line. The sync removes
# them from this repository on every run, so a path that is here is
# a divergence from the rule that these trees are upstream's, minus
# The drift check reads this list: a file upstream holds under one of
# these paths is not a file the copy is missing, and one of them that
# is here is a file the copy should not have. The list is written
# here, by the sync, so there is one answer to what is excluded.
